entries.claim: JPMorgan rebranded its blockchain unit from Onyx to 'Kinexys by J.P. Morgan' (announced 6 November 2024), renaming JPM Coin System to Kinexys Digital Payments and Onyx Digital Assets to Kinexys Digital Assets, and creating Kinexys Labs.
JPM Coin (launched 2019) is a tokenised USD deposit supporting programmable features: conditional release, scheduled transfers and rule-based payments.
Kinexys Digital Payments runs on a permissioned, EVM-compatible ledger using Blockchain Deposit Accounts (BDAs), supporting USD/EUR/GBP with on-chain FX (USD/EUR).
Kinexys is described as using an asynchronous dual-ledger bridge architecture, with the ledger running parallel to JPMorgan's core banking systems and synced via event-driven APIs.
In 2025 JPMorgan issued a USD deposit token (JPMD) on Base, a public Ethereum Layer 2, for institutional clients, becoming the first bank to do so.
Kinexys operates a Tokenized Collateral Network (TCN) and an intraday repo product enabling secured intraday financing against tokenised collateral.
Kinexys averages approximately $7 billion in daily transaction volume with over $4 trillion in cumulative transactions since inception (self-reported).
entries.source_ref: JPMorgan press/newsroom and HBS case study (2025-2026)

entries.claim: JPMorgan Payments processes approximately $12 trillion in payments per average day (self-reported).

For FY2025 (year ended 31 December 2025), JPMorgan Chase reported ROE of 17%, CET1 capital ratio (Standardized) of 14.5-14.6%, Tier 1 capital ratio of 15.5%, average loans of ~$1.5T and average deposits of ~$2.6T.
entries.source_ref: JPMorgan Chase FY2025 Annual Report / 4Q25 Financial Results (investor-relations PDFs)

entries.claim: Named Kinexys Digital Payments participants include DBS, Siemens, FedEx, BlackRock, Barclays, Trafigura, LSEG SwapAgent and Ondo Finance (third-party compilation).
The consensus/validator governance of the Kinexys permissioned ledger and the source code of its smart contracts (programmable payments, repo) are not public.
